Flaky Test Tracker

Reference·seedling·JUL 30, 2026

A backlog of flaky tests — e2e (Cucumber + Playwright) and unit (vitest). Drop a row when you hit one; an agent clears the queue from time to time.

Contents

  • Flake vs. break
  • Backlog
  • Logging a flake
  • Fixing routine
  • Common flake classes

A fix-queue for tests that go red on one CI run and green on the next with no code change. See a flake → add a row. An agent works the backlog over time.

Flake vs. break

A flake fails nondeterministically — timing, ordering, or environment — and would pass on a same-SHA rerun; a break fails the same way every run and is a real defect, so file a bug instead. A one-off rerun via the odu MCP is fine to triage which it is — but a rerun is never how a flake gets fixed (see the routine below).

Backlog

Status: open → fixing → fixed (then strike the row).

Queue clear — the eight below were fixed in #1440 (struck = done; the reusable patterns live in Common flake classes).

Test Lane Symptom Repro’d in Status Fix
Biome format/lint survives the Home Manager VM fan-out (ci::fmt, ci::biome) fmt@x86_64-linux / biome@x86_64-linux After the nixpkgs advance, Biome crashed only while idli’s Home Manager lane was running its QEMU fan-out: two full lint runs, one immediate lint rerun, and the next run’s formatter ended via SIGSEGV, SIGABRT (memory allocation of 56 bytes failed), or SIGILL. The exact same Biome 2.4.15 binary linted all 1530 files in 471ms on the unchanged idli worktree once the VM fan-out drained; every non-Biome node was green. The DAG now places both Biome consumers after home-manager, removing the overlap instead of retrying it or reverting the toolchain. Recurred at 1ea67bc (#2019) — and the DAG fix is intact; a manual node_rerun walks around it. ci::home-manager failed first (Nix daemon disconnected unexpectedly), I re-ran that single node, and the re-run put the QEMU fan-out back in parallel with the Biome consumers the #1988 ordering exists to keep clear of it — ci::biome then died by SIGSEGV and ci::fmt by memory allocation of 30 bytes failed, the same signature as the original row. The ordering constraint lives in the DAG, so it governs a fresh run’s schedule and not an out-of-band single-node re-run: re-running an upstream node re-introduces exactly the overlap the fix removed. Practical rule this yields — when the first red is ci::home-manager, restart the RUN rather than re-running the node, or the next two reds are manufactured by the retry itself. Compounded here by the box: all six kolu-ci-* were down (ssh unreachable), forcing the lane onto the shared idli-01 workstation, so the memory headroom the overlap needed was not there either. REOPENED — recurred at 32006b5 (#2011) on a leased pool box. biome lint died by signal 11 with Biome’s own internal-error banner (“This is a bug in Biome, not an error in your code”), assertion left == right failed at crates/biome_rowan/src/tree_builder.rs:209 on thread biome::workspace_worker_5. Same crash-in-the-linter class as the original row, and same disposition: a same-SHA node_rerun of ci::biome@x86_64-linux passed, and the identical lint is green locally on the same tree. So the earlier fix did not close this class — worth reading as box/lane contention rather than as repository content, since the input is unchanged between the crash and the green rerun. #1988, #2019 open #1988 (DAG order); re-run hazard noted at #2019
The whole x86_64-linux pool is down, silently demoting CI onto a shared workstation *@x86_64-linux just ci::pool-status reported 0 healthy of 8 (kolu-ci-1..8, every one ssh-unreachable: failed to start SSH connection), so odu leased the fallback idli-01 — a shared 32-core workstation also carrying other agent sessions. Nothing announces the demotion: the run starts, lanes green, and only the memory-shaped reds (Nix daemon disconnected, biome SIGSEGV, memory allocation of 30 bytes failed) say the box is starved. This is the box-capacity reading the Code-tab row below already reached — “the durable fix is running e2e on a free pool box … not hardening the locator” — arriving again from the other direction, so it is recorded here as its own row rather than as another test’s flake. just ci::pool-ensure is the documented repair. #2019 open —
padi unit lane dies on a vitest worker fork exiting at teardown (ci::unit) unit@x86_64-linux Every test PASSED — 52 test files (1 skipped), 392 tests (23 skipped) — and the lane still failed, on an Unhandled Error raised AFTER the run: [vitest-pool]: Worker forks emitted error / Worker exited unexpectedly from ChildProcess.emitUnexpectedExit. Cleared on a same-SHA node_rerun (47 s, green), on a 32-core box (idli-01) where vitest fans out widely — consistent with a teardown/resource race rather than a code fault. Change-independent: #1982 touches padi’s port scan, whose only surviving handles there are unref-ed timers, which cannot hold a worker open or kill it. #1982 open —

Actionable reading: this row is a box-capacity symptom, not a test bug — the durable fix is running e2e on a free pool box (all kolu-ci-* were down that day, forcing the workstation), not hardening the locator. File-drop / clipboard path reaches the PTY (file-drop.feature:10+:14, clipboard.feature:9) e2e (both) the screen state should contain "<file>" → 20s waitForFunction timeout. Root cause is the screen-state reader, not delivery: the DIAG dump shows both scratch/write + sendInput sent, no toast, and the filename fully on screen — but the long W2.2 scratch path ($XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/kolu-<pid>/scratch/<uuid>/<name>, ~81 chars) hard-wraps at the 80-col grid before xterm’s fit() widens it under load, so the filename straddles the wrap (…no+tes.md). __readXtermBuffer joined rows with \n, splitting the match. The W2.2 padi-state-root cutover lengthened the path past the old short-runtimeDir mitigation; the bash “garbles the cells” note in hooks.ts was a mis-diagnosis (cells are clean). Fix: __readXtermBuffer rejoins isWrapped continuation rows into one logical line, so a straddling filename matches regardless of width/path-length. Verified 10/10 under CPU oversubscription that gave ~100% failure pre-fix (leased kolu-ci-1). #1664 fixed #1664

Logging a flake

When a lane goes red and a single-node rerun comes back green, add a row: test name, recipe@platform lane, the assertion/timeout, the PR it reproduced in (<PrLink pr={…} />), open. No investigation needed to log it.

Keep the tracker in lock-step with your PR. Log a flake your CI surfaced in the same PR that hit it — don’t defer to a later cleanup; and a PR that fixes a flake flips its row to fixed (and strikes it) in that same PR, regenerating docs/atlas/dist/. The queue only stays trustworthy if every PR that touches a flake updates this note alongside its own diff.

Fixing routine

An agent clears the backlog by driving CI to N consecutive green runs (N = 5 by default, or as given) through the odu MCP (run the test lanes → wait_for_settle, repeated). The green streak verifies that a fix is real — it is never a way to wash a flake out.

Non-negotiable rules:

  • A single failure is a fix, not a re-run. One red lane → stop and fix the root cause. Re-running to hope for green is forbidden, and any failure resets the streak to 0.
  • Fix the test, not the app. A flake is a defect in the test; change only packages/tests, never application code — unless a fix is provably impossible without it.
  • Kill the timing dependence, don’t pad it. A “timing issue” is fixed by waiting on a deterministic signal (a real DOM/aria state, an app event, an awaited promise, correct setup ordering) — never by bumping a timeout or adding a sleep.
  • Reuse past de-flake PRs. Read how this suite was de-flaked before — start from Common flake classes below — and apply the established pattern instead of inventing one.
  • Code changes pass /agent-debate before the streak counts. Batch the fixes, then drive them through /agent-debate with an explicitly selected peer to consensus — a CI pass is only trusted on agent-debate-passed commits (docs are exempt, and the debate is expensive, so debate the batch, not each edit). The peer inspects read-only while the author applies agreed fixes, but consensus still needs CI verification: defend an empirically-grounded fix rather than concede a plausible-but-unverified simplification — a consensus that contradicts an observed CI failure is wrong until CI proves otherwise.

The loop: fail → streak resets to 0, root-cause and fix the test (fixing → fixed, link the PR with <PrLink pr={…} />); while there, drop any open row that no longer reproduces. Pass → streak +1. Done = N green runs back-to-back with the backlog cleared.

Common flake classes

The shapes this suite keeps throwing, and the fix that held — reach for these before inventing one (full detail in each linked PR / the fix’s code comment).

  • darwin drops a second fs event. An append or a 2nd create (a transcript append, a <pid>.json after its dir) is the event FSEvents/inotify drops under parallel-worker load, so the watcher never re-fires. Fix: write data-then-trigger (the reliable first event carries the payload), or nudgeFiles the path every poll tick (tests/support/nudge.ts) to re-fire the watch. (claude-code.feature:77)
  • A one-shot resolve against a stream’s first snapshot can’t recover. If a consumer resolves once on the first !pending() frame and the stream won’t re-yield (state already settled), a stale first snapshot is permanent — no marker barrier saves it. Fix: warm / mount the source first so it has enumerated before the action. (file-ref-link.feature:69)
  • A baseline recorded mid-settle drifts. Recording a transform/value while an animation or a sensor re-resolve is in flight captures a moving target. Fix: settle-before-baseline — wait on the steady-state signal (tile centered, git settled to the repo, tree row enumerated) before recording or asserting. (canvas.feature:161, code-tab.feature:714)
  • A passive reader observes a half-built git state. A gitStatus first read can tear the stream down for good on BASE_BRANCH_NOT_FOUND if it lands between repo-init and base-ref creation. Fix: make the base ref exist atomically (seed a bare origin, then git clone) and do setup in a subshell so the terminal’s cwd never enters the in-between repo. (code-tab.feature:148)
  • Faking occlusion by swallowing render output leaks. Suppressing refreshRows still lets an incidental sync paint through. Fix: model the real freeze — park requestAnimationFrame so only a forced sync repaint counts. (render_recovery.feature:16)
  • An edge-triggered effect can’t re-assert after a non-change (app fix). Focus stolen by a transient element when the reactive focused state didn’t change leaves the edge effect unfired. Fix: bump a level nonce the handler increments so the effect re-asserts. (sub-terminal.feature:107)
  • Polling a live, reconciling collection throws transients (esp. vitest — no retry). A poll hits transient stream errors as the collection settles or a key reconciles out mid-read. Fix: catch-and-retry in the poll, and skip a key that vanishes between keys() and get() — the snapshot helper owns the narrow suppression, the poller stays a pure condition-checker. (daemon.test.ts)
  • A screen-state match string that hard-wraps at the grid edge is split by the reader. xterm wraps a logical line longer than cols across rows; a reader that joins rows with \n inserts a newline INSIDE the wrapped token, so a substring check (includes("notes.md")) misses it even though the text is fully on screen. Flakes because the wrap column depends on content length and on fit() having widened the grid past the 80-col default — which lags under load. Fix: rejoin isWrapped continuation rows into one logical line in the buffer reader (__readXtermBuffer), trimming right only at the logical-line end. Width- and path-length-independent — never a timeout bump. (file-drop.feature, clipboard.feature)
